issue.title: [rcl_yaml_param_parser] Heap-buffer-overflow in namespace handling (add_name_to_ns / rem_name_from_ns)
issue.bodyHTML:
Generated by Generative AI

No response

Operating System:

Ubuntu 22.04

ROS version or commit hash:

90f18f3

RMW implementation (if applicable):

No response

RMW Configuration (if applicable):

No response

Client library (if applicable):

rcl_yaml_param_parser

'ros2 doctor --report' output

ros2 doctor --report 
<COPY OUTPUT HERE>

Steps to reproduce issue

I wrote a simple libFuzzer target that:

  1. Writes fuzz data to a temporary file.
  2. Calls rcl_parse_yaml_file() on that file.
  3. Cleans up and returns.

Roughly:

extern "C" int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *data, size_t size)
{
  if (size == 0) {
    return 0;
  }

  rcutils_allocator_t allocator = rcutils_get_default_allocator();
  rcl_params_t * params = rcl_yaml_node_struct_init(allocator);
  if (!params) {
    return 0;
  }

  char filename[] = "/tmp/ros2_yaml_fuzz_XXXXXX";
  int fd = mkstemp(filename);
  if (fd < 0) {
    rcl_yaml_node_struct_fini(params);
    return 0;
  }

  (void)write(fd, data, size);
  close(fd);

  (void)rcl_parse_yaml_file(filename, params);

  unlink(filename);
  rcl_yaml_node_struct_fini(params);
  return 0;
}

Running this fuzzer with ASan enabled produces a crashing input (crash-224ea443c392611a4695d18acc9080b0fa96976b) that triggers the heap-buffer-overflow inside the namespace handling code.

ASan report (trimmed)

Key part of the AddressSanitizer output:

=================================================================
==18==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x7bb86e3eb94f at pc 0x56195870b0f5 bp 0x7ffdabccd590 sp 0x7ffdabcccd38
READ of size 1 at 0x7bb86e3eb94f thread T0

    #0 0x56195870b0f4 in strcmp
       /src/llvm-project/compiler-rt/lib/asan/../sanitizer_common/sanitizer_common_interceptors.inc:505:5
    #1 0x5619587e6dbc in add_name_to_ns
       /src/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser/src/namespace.c:68:9
    #2 0x5619587e2af4 in parse_key
       /src/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser/src/parse.c:792:17
    #3 0x5619587e48e2 in parse_file_events
       /src/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser/src/parse.c:950:19

    #5 0x5619587d7951 in LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput
       /src/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser_fuzzer.cc:116:9
    ...

0x7bb86e3eb94f is located 1 bytes before 1-byte region [0x7bb86e3eb950,0x7bb86e3eb951)
allocated by thread T0 here:

    #0 0x561958793bbc in realloc
       /src/llvm-project/compiler-rt/lib/asan/asan_malloc_linux.cpp:81:3
    #1 0x5619587e7463 in rem_name_from_ns
       /src/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser/src/namespace.c:144:29
    #2 0x5619587e4c1a in parse_file_events
       /src/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser/src/parse.c:1033:19
    #3 0x5619587d94f2 in rcl_parse_yaml_file
       /src/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser/src/parser.c:279:23
    #4 0x5619587d7951 in LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput
       /src/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser_fuzzer.cc:116:9
    ...

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow
  /src/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser/src/namespace.c:68:9 in add_name_to_ns
=================================================================

So:

  • The read OOB is in add_name_to_ns() at namespace.c:68.
  • The allocation of the offending 1-byte buffer is in rem_name_from_ns() at namespace.c:144.

Expected behavior

Relevant code: add_name_to_ns

File: rcl_yaml_param_parser/src/namespace.c

rcutils_ret_t add_name_to_ns(
  namespace_tracker_t * ns_tracker,
  const char * name,
  const namespace_type_t namespace_type,
  rcutils_allocator_t allocator)
{
  char * cur_ns;
  uint32_t * cur_count;
  char * sep_str;
  size_t name_len;
  size_t ns_len;
  size_t sep_len;
  size_t tot_len;

  switch (namespace_type) {
    case NS_TYPE_NODE:
      cur_ns = ns_tracker->node_ns;
      cur_count = &(ns_tracker->num_node_ns);
      sep_str = NODE_NS_SEPERATOR;
      break;
    case NS_TYPE_PARAM:
      cur_ns = ns_tracker->parameter_ns;
      cur_count = &(ns_tracker->num_parameter_ns);
      sep_str = PARAMETER_NS_SEPERATOR;
      break;
    default:
      return RCUTILS_RET_ERROR;
  }

  /// Add a name to ns
  if (NULL == name) {
    return RCUTILS_RET_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
  }
  if (0U == *cur_count) {
    cur_ns = rcutils_strdup(name, allocator);
    if (NULL == cur_ns) {
      return RCUTILS_RET_BAD_ALLOC;
    }
  } else {
    ns_len = strlen(cur_ns);
    name_len = strlen(name);
    sep_len = strlen(sep_str);
    // Check the last sep_len characters of the current NS against the separator string.
    if (strcmp(cur_ns + ns_len - sep_len, sep_str) == 0) {
      // Current NS already ends with the separator: don't put another separator in.
      sep_len = 0;
      sep_str = "";
    }

    tot_len = ns_len + sep_len + name_len + 1U;

    char * tmp_ns_ptr = allocator.reallocate(cur_ns, tot_len, allocator.state);
    if (NULL == tmp_ns_ptr) {
      return RCUTILS_RET_BAD_ALLOC;
    }
    cur_ns = tmp_ns_ptr;
    memcpy((cur_ns + ns_len), sep_str, sep_len);
    memcpy((cur_ns + ns_len + sep_len), name, name_len);
    cur_ns[tot_len - 1U] = '\0';
  }
  *cur_count = (*cur_count + 1U);

  if (NS_TYPE_NODE == namespace_type) {
    ns_tracker->node_ns = cur_ns;
  } else {
    ns_tracker->parameter_ns = cur_ns;
  }
  return RCUTILS_RET_OK;
}

The critical line is:

if (strcmp(cur_ns + ns_len - sep_len, sep_str) == 0) {

This assumes that ns_len >= sep_len. If ns_len < sep_len, the expression cur_ns + ns_len - sep_len points before the allocated buffer, which is exactly what ASan reports.

Actual behavior

Relevant code: rem_name_from_ns

Also in rcl_yaml_param_parser/src/namespace.c:

rcutils_ret_t rem_name_from_ns(
  namespace_tracker_t * ns_tracker,
  const namespace_type_t namespace_type,
  rcutils_allocator_t allocator)
{
  char * cur_ns;
  uint32_t * cur_count;
  char * sep_str;
  size_t ns_len;
  size_t tot_len;

  switch (namespace_type) {
    case NS_TYPE_NODE:
      cur_ns = ns_tracker->node_ns;
      cur_count = &(ns_tracker->num_node_ns);
      sep_str = NODE_NS_SEPERATOR;
      break;
    case NS_TYPE_PARAM:
      cur_ns = ns_tracker->parameter_ns;
      cur_count = &(ns_tracker->num_parameter_ns);
      sep_str = PARAMETER_NS_SEPERATOR;
      break;
    default:
      return RCUTILS_RET_ERROR;
  }

  /// Remove last name from ns
  if (*cur_count > 0U) {
    if (1U == *cur_count) {
      allocator.deallocate(cur_ns, allocator.state);
      cur_ns = NULL;
    } else {
      ns_len = strlen(cur_ns);
      char * last_idx = NULL;
      char * next_str = NULL;
      const char * end_ptr = (cur_ns + ns_len);

      next_str = strstr(cur_ns, sep_str);
      while (NULL != next_str) {
        if (next_str > end_ptr) {
          RCUTILS_SET_ERROR_MSG("Internal error. Crossing array boundary");
          return RCUTILS_RET_ERROR;
        }
        last_idx = next_str;
        next_str = (next_str + strlen(sep_str));
        next_str = strstr(next_str, sep_str);
      }
      if (NULL != last_idx) {
        tot_len = ((size_t)(last_idx - cur_ns) + 1U);
        char * tmp_ns_ptr = allocator.reallocate(cur_ns, tot_len, allocator.state);
        if (NULL == tmp_ns_ptr) {
          return RCUTILS_RET_BAD_ALLOC;
        }
        cur_ns = tmp_ns_ptr;
        cur_ns[tot_len - 1U] = '\0';
      }
    }
    *cur_count = (*cur_count - 1U);
  }
  if (NS_TYPE_NODE == namespace_type) {
    ns_tracker->node_ns = cur_ns;
  } else {
    ns_tracker->parameter_ns = cur_ns;
  }
  return RCUTILS_RET_OK;
}

In some cases, last_idx can be equal to cur_ns (e.g., if the only occurrence of the separator is at the very beginning of the string). Then:

  • tot_len = (last_idx - cur_ns) + 1U = 1
  • reallocate(cur_ns, 1) returns a 1-byte buffer
  • cur_ns[0] = '\0' → cur_ns becomes an empty string ""
  • *cur_count is decremented but remains > 0

So it is possible for the internal state to become:

  • cur_ns points to a 1-byte, empty string.
  • *cur_count > 0.

On the next call to add_name_to_ns(), this causes the else branch to run with ns_len == 0, which then hits strcmp(cur_ns + ns_len - sep_len, sep_str) with sep_len >= 1, thus reading before the buffer.

Additional information

Root cause

The bug stems from two combined issues:

  1. Unsafe pointer arithmetic in add_name_to_ns()
    add_name_to_ns() assumes that when *cur_count > 0, the namespace string is at least as long as the separator:
if (strcmp(cur_ns + ns_len - sep_len, sep_str) == 0)

This is not guarded by ns_len >= sep_len, leading to a left-of-buffer read if ns_len < sep_len.

  1. Inconsistent internal state in rem_name_from_ns()
    rem_name_from_ns() can shrink cur_ns to an empty string while leaving *cur_count > 0 (e.g., when the last separator is at the start of the string). This violates the implicit invariant that “*cur_count > 0 ⇒ cur_ns non-empty and at least sep_len long”.

Together these lead to the reported heap-buffer-overflow.

Possible fix ideas

At a minimum, the add_name_to_ns() separator check should guard against ns_len < sep_len:

ns_len = strlen(cur_ns);
name_len = strlen(name);
sep_len = strlen(sep_str);

if (sep_len > 0 && ns_len >= sep_len &&
    strcmp(cur_ns + ns_len - sep_len, sep_str) == 0) {
  sep_len = 0;
  sep_str = "";
}

Additionally, it may be worthwhile to tighten the invariants in rem_name_from_ns() so that the string and count remain consistent. For example, when last_idx == cur_ns (no remaining name parts after removing the last one), we could explicitly reset the namespace:

  • either free and set the pointer to NULL and the count to 0, or
  • keep an empty string but set the count to 0.

That way, add_name_to_ns() will not enter the “existing namespace” branch with an empty namespace.

Thanks for taking a look and for providing the test_params.yaml / repro code.

I’ve re-verified the issue and can confirm the following:

  • With the real rmw_validate_* implementations in a normal ROS 2 setup, invalid names like /: (empty node name) are rejected and I see an error instead of a crash – as you observed.
  • The heap-buffer-overflow is triggered when rcl_yaml_param_parser is used with permissive rmw_\* stubs (i.e., rmw_validate_* always returns “valid”), which is how I am fuzzing the library in isolation.

To make this concrete, here is a standalone reproducer that uses the same rmw_\* stubs as my OSS-Fuzz harness and calls rcl_parse_yaml_file() directly.

Standalone reproducer (poc.cc)

// poc.cc - standalone reproducer for heap-buffer-overflow in
// rcl_yaml_param_parser namespace handling, using the same rmw_* stubs
// as the OSS-Fuzz harness.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>

#include <fcntl.h>
#include <unistd.h>

extern "C" {
#include "rcl_yaml_param_parser/parser.h"
#include "rcutils/allocator.h"

#include "rmw/validate_namespace.h"
#include "rmw/validate_node_name.h"
#include "rmw/types.h"
#include "rmw/error_handling.h"
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// rmw stubs used by rcl_yaml_param_parser (same as fuzz harness)
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extern "C" rmw_ret_t
rmw_validate_namespace(const char * namespace_,
                       int * validation_result,
                       size_t * invalid_index)
{
  if (!namespace_ || !validation_result) {
    return RMW_RET_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
  }
  *validation_result = RMW_NAMESPACE_VALID;
  if (invalid_index) {
    *invalid_index = 0;
  }
  return RMW_RET_OK;
}

extern "C" rmw_ret_t
rmw_validate_namespace_with_size(const char * namespace_,
                                 size_t /*namespace_length*/,
                                 int * validation_result,
                                 size_t * invalid_index)
{
  return rmw_validate_namespace(namespace_, validation_result, invalid_index);
}

extern "C" const char *
rmw_namespace_validation_result_string(int /*validation_result*/)
{
  return "stub-namespace-validation";
}

extern "C" rmw_ret_t
rmw_validate_node_name(const char * node_name,
                       int * validation_result,
                       size_t * invalid_index)
{
  if (!node_name || !validation_result) {
    return RMW_RET_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
  }
  *validation_result = RMW_NODE_NAME_VALID;
  if (invalid_index) {
    *invalid_index = 0;
  }
  return RMW_RET_OK;
}

extern "C" rmw_ret_t
rmw_validate_node_name_with_size(const char * node_name,
                                 size_t /*node_name_length*/,
                                 int * validation_result,
                                 size_t * invalid_index)
{
  return rmw_validate_node_name(node_name, validation_result, invalid_index);
}

extern "C" const char *
rmw_node_name_validation_result_string(int /*validation_result*/)
{
  return "stub-node-name-validation";
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Simple main() that calls rcl_parse_yaml_file on a user-supplied YAML file
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
  if (argc != 2) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s <yaml-file>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }

  const char * filename = argv[1];

  rcutils_allocator_t allocator = rcutils_get_default_allocator();
  rcl_params_t * params = rcl_yaml_node_struct_init(allocator);
  if (!params) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "rcl_yaml_node_struct_init failed\n");
    return 1;
  }

  // This is where the bug is triggered for the crashing YAML.
  (void)rcl_parse_yaml_file(filename, params);

  rcl_yaml_node_struct_fini(params);
  return 0;
}

Summary / impact

So to clarify the situation:

  • With real rmw_validate_* in a normal ROS 2 deployment, invalid node names / namespaces are rejected and the parser returns an error. In that configuration, this heap-buffer-overflow appears unreachable.
  • With permissive or stubbed rmw_validate_* (as in my fuzz harness and the above poc.cc), it is possible for:
    • rem_name_from_ns() to leave cur_ns as a 1-byte empty string ("") while *cur_count > 0, and then
    • add_name_to_ns() to execute: if (strcmp(cur_ns + ns_len - sep_len, sep_str) == 0) { with ns_len == 0, sep_len == 1, producing the out-of-bounds read reported by ASan.

From a security / user impact point of view, I agree this is likely not exploitable in normal ROS 2 usage as long as rmw_validate_* enforces the intended naming rules.

However, it is still a real memory-safety issue in rcl_yaml_param_parser when used with different or stubbed rmw implementations (e.g., in tests, fuzzers, or alternative environments), and it stems from an internal invariant mismatch between rem_name_from_ns() and add_name_to_ns().

That’s why I still think the small hardening changes discussed earlier (guarding ns_len >= sep_len in add_name_to_ns() and ensuring rem_name_from_ns() does not leave cur_ns="" with *cur_count > 0) would be worthwhile, even if you classify this as a robustness fix rather than a user-visible crash in the default configuration.

Thanks for taking a look and for providing the test_params.yaml / repro code.

I’ve re-verified the issue and can confirm the following:

  • With the real rmw_validate_* implementations in a normal ROS 2 setup, invalid names like /: (empty node name) are rejected and I see an error instead of a crash – as you observed.
  • The heap-buffer-overflow is triggered when rcl_yaml_param_parser is used with permissive rmw_\* stubs (i.e., rmw_validate_* always returns “valid”), which is how I am fuzzing the library in isolation.

To make this concrete, here is a standalone reproducer that uses the same rmw_\* stubs as my OSS-Fuzz harness and calls rcl_parse_yaml_file() directly.

Standalone reproducer (poc.cc)

// poc.cc - standalone reproducer for heap-buffer-overflow in
// rcl_yaml_param_parser namespace handling, using the same rmw_* stubs
// as the OSS-Fuzz harness.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>

#include <fcntl.h>
#include <unistd.h>

extern "C" {
#include "rcl_yaml_param_parser/parser.h"
#include "rcutils/allocator.h"

#include "rmw/validate_namespace.h"
#include "rmw/validate_node_name.h"
#include "rmw/types.h"
#include "rmw/error_handling.h"
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// rmw stubs used by rcl_yaml_param_parser (same as fuzz harness)
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extern "C" rmw_ret_t
rmw_validate_namespace(const char * namespace_,
                       int * validation_result,
                       size_t * invalid_index)
{
  if (!namespace_ || !validation_result) {
    return RMW_RET_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
  }
  *validation_result = RMW_NAMESPACE_VALID;
  if (invalid_index) {
    *invalid_index = 0;
  }
  return RMW_RET_OK;
}

extern "C" rmw_ret_t
rmw_validate_namespace_with_size(const char * namespace_,
                                 size_t /*namespace_length*/,
                                 int * validation_result,
                                 size_t * invalid_index)
{
  return rmw_validate_namespace(namespace_, validation_result, invalid_index);
}

extern "C" const char *
rmw_namespace_validation_result_string(int /*validation_result*/)
{
  return "stub-namespace-validation";
}

extern "C" rmw_ret_t
rmw_validate_node_name(const char * node_name,
                       int * validation_result,
                       size_t * invalid_index)
{
  if (!node_name || !validation_result) {
    return RMW_RET_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
  }
  *validation_result = RMW_NODE_NAME_VALID;
  if (invalid_index) {
    *invalid_index = 0;
  }
  return RMW_RET_OK;
}

extern "C" rmw_ret_t
rmw_validate_node_name_with_size(const char * node_name,
                                 size_t /*node_name_length*/,
                                 int * validation_result,
                                 size_t * invalid_index)
{
  return rmw_validate_node_name(node_name, validation_result, invalid_index);
}

extern "C" const char *
rmw_node_name_validation_result_string(int /*validation_result*/)
{
  return "stub-node-name-validation";
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Simple main() that calls rcl_parse_yaml_file on a user-supplied YAML file
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
  if (argc != 2) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s <yaml-file>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }

  const char * filename = argv[1];

  rcutils_allocator_t allocator = rcutils_get_default_allocator();
  rcl_params_t * params = rcl_yaml_node_struct_init(allocator);
  if (!params) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "rcl_yaml_node_struct_init failed\n");
    return 1;
  }

  // This is where the bug is triggered for the crashing YAML.
  (void)rcl_parse_yaml_file(filename, params);

  rcl_yaml_node_struct_fini(params);
  return 0;
}

Build & run (in the same OSS-Fuzz-style environment)

Inside the same container where I built the fuzzer (with build.sh), I compile:

  -I/src/rcl/rcl_yaml_param_parser/include \
  -I/src/rcutils/include \
  -I/src/rmw/rmw/include \
  /poc/poc.cc \
  /work/rcl_yaml_param_parser_build/librcl_yaml_param_parser.a \
  /work/rcutils_build/librcutils.a \
  -lyaml \
  -o /poc/rcl_yaml_ns_repro

Then run against the crashing YAML:

Target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

root@3d699b09fe39:/poc# clang++ --version
clang version 22.0.0git (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project.git cb2f0d0a5f14c183e7182aba0f0e54a518de9e3f)
Target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

Summary / impact

So to clarify the situation:

  • With real rmw_validate_* in a normal ROS 2 deployment, invalid node names / namespaces are rejected and the parser returns an error. In that configuration, this heap-buffer-overflow appears unreachable.
  • With permissive or stubbed rmw_validate_* (as in my fuzz harness and the above poc.cc), it is possible for:
    • rem_name_from_ns() to leave cur_ns as a 1-byte empty string ("") while *cur_count > 0, and then
    • add_name_to_ns() to execute: if (strcmp(cur_ns + ns_len - sep_len, sep_str) == 0) { with ns_len == 0, sep_len == 1, producing the out-of-bounds read reported by ASan.

From a security / user impact point of view, I agree this is likely not exploitable in normal ROS 2 usage as long as rmw_validate_* enforces the intended naming rules.

However, it is still a real memory-safety issue in rcl_yaml_param_parser when used with different or stubbed rmw implementations (e.g., in tests, fuzzers, or alternative environments), and it stems from an internal invariant mismatch between rem_name_from_ns() and add_name_to_ns().

That’s why I still think the small hardening changes discussed earlier (guarding ns_len >= sep_len in add_name_to_ns() and ensuring rem_name_from_ns() does not leave cur_ns="" with *cur_count > 0) would be worthwhile, even if you classify this as a robustness fix rather than a user-visible crash in the default configuration.
